**JIRA-001 backend (4h) goes to Drew (agent-002).**
- This ticket is collaboration-heavy.
- Reese cannot handle synchronous coordination this week.
- Drew is the other backend specialist and has exactly 4 hours free.

**JIRA-002 backend (4h) goes to Reese (agent-003).**
- This ticket is low priority and not collaboration-heavy, so it fits Reese's constraint.
- Reese has exactly 4 hours available.

**JIRA-001 QA (3h) goes to Robin (agent-004). Please review this one.**
- Robin prefers not to take this collaboration-heavy QA work.
- Robin is the only QA specialist on the team and has exactly the 3 hours needed.
- I treated the preference as soft rather than leave a medium-priority ticket without QA coverage.
- You may want to talk with Robin, or find QA support from outside the team, if the preference should be honored.

**JIRA-003 security (2h) goes to Kai (agent-005).** Kai is the security specialist and has 2 hours available.

**JIRA-004 frontend (3h) goes to Avi (agent-007).** Avi is the frontend specialist and has 3 hours available.

**JIRA-005 data (2h) goes to Riley (agent-008).** Riley is the data specialist and has 2 hours available.

**Other notes**
- Quinn (UX, 2h) has no assignment because no ticket needs UX work.
- Every assignment matches the person's specialty and fits within their available hours.
- None of the tickets has a sensitive-data surface.
